note.saw: Nothing yet: this is the very first build of the piece.
note.changing: Lays down the whole composition at once: wobbling tunnel rings, a honeycomb membrane with eyes in its cells, the salmon in sockeye colors pushed to neon, a small chrysanthemum at the vortex core and the name arching overhead in rainbow letters.
note.why: A salmon is the fish that fights its way upstream, and a vortex of water is the most natural portal for it to leap through.
note.idea: A hook-jawed spawning salmon leaps on a diagonal out of a liquid hyperspace vortex; the splash explodes into fractal droplets with eyes and mandalas inside, and the name arcs over the top on a breaking wave crest.

note.saw: The background was far too sparse, with wide dark tunnel bands and empty honeycomb, and the salmon's body was flat magenta and nearly straight, more glide than leap.
note.changing: Fills the tunnel with finer rings and dotted echoes, a smaller honeycomb, alien glyph script, marbled currents, corner paisleys and a big chrysanthemum at the core; the salmon gets rainbow bands of eyed scales and more of an arch.
note.why: DMT space has no empty corners, so every surface should feel alive.

note.saw: The paisleys came out jagged and blocky, the currents wandered like random spaghetti across the tunnel, the ribbon's right curl hid the hooked snout, and the splash was a cluttered clump.
note.changing: Redraws the paisleys with smooth edges, makes the currents follow the tunnel's rings, tucks the ribbon behind the salmon so the hooked jaw shows, and wraps the fish in a dark moat inside its gold glow.
note.why: The fish has to separate from the busy water, and the water has to move in one direction.

note.saw: There was no light at the end of the tunnel, no mid-sized repeats of the core flower, and the fins had no fluid edges.
note.changing: Sends swirling light beams out of the core, scatters eleven smaller chrysanthemums through the walls, brightens the honeycomb, tries liquid curls along the edges of the tail and dorsal fin, and starts the splash jets along the tail's trailing edge.
note.why: A tunnel needs a light to fall toward, and the same flower at three sizes is the self-similar feeling of the trip.

note.saw: The background was one even mid-sized texture with no big sweeping forms, so the vortex read weakly and the eye had nowhere to travel.
note.changing: Adds five big rainbow liquid arms spiralling out of the core, each a wide tapering ribbon of nested color bands with a bead row; in this first try they shoot out almost straight.
note.why: The eye needs a large flow to travel along.

note.saw: The splash jets crossed the core chrysanthemum and buried its centre, which was only a plain dot, and the arms curled off the edge of the badge.
note.changing: Lifts the core flower on top of the splash, drops the jets that crossed it, and gives its centre a spiral-web portal eye in a white bloom; the arms are re-aimed to curl inside the badge with a little wobble.
note.why: The core is where the light comes from, so it should be a portal.

note.saw: The droplets were cobalt on a cobalt ground, so the splash still read weakly at full size.
note.changing: Recolors the droplets white-to-cyan, makes them bigger, and adds a backlight glowing behind the tail.
note.why: Water should catch the light.

note.saw: SavesFish asked for a much more legible name, and the artist's lettering was small, with a rainbow gradient and a 3D stack, exactly the things that make a word muddy.
note.changing: Rebuilds SAVESFISH in big solid cream capitals over a thick ink outline, with a cyan neon rim and a soft magenta glow, on a widened calm dark band along the wave crest.
note.why: The name has to read instantly at badge size.

note.saw: The second artist inherits the finished first draft and has not yet looked at it closely.
note.changing: Nothing: the draft is rendered again exactly as it was, pixel for pixel, to study at full size, at badge size and up close.
note.why: An honest look at the untouched piece is the baseline for deciding how deep the second pass needs to go.
note.idea: Make the whole background one liquid field of swirling rainbow contour bands, redraw the salmon as a deep-bodied male sockeye in a real leaping arch with warm spawning colors on cool water, and turn the splash into a crown of liquid around a glowing core.

note.saw: With fresh eyes, the first draft was a collage of equal-weight stickers, so the vortex never read; the salmon was a thin rainbow-striped tube that looked like a trout, and the colors were mid-blue mush under a milky haze.
note.changing: A rewrite: the background becomes one liquid field of rainbow contour bands with bead rows, glyph script and watching eyes, and the salmon becomes a deep-bodied male sockeye mid-leap, with a spawning hump, toothed hooked jaw, green head, crimson body and gold belly. The core is now a glowing honeycomb funnel with a chrysanthemum and a pinwheel of jets.
note.why: In this group everything has to flow, so the water itself became the picture; and a salmon is only iconic when you can see the hump, the hooked jaw and the red-and-green spawning colors.

note.saw: The salmon now read instantly even at thumbnail size, but the core was a pale blue disc whose white jets looked like a ribcage, the honeycomb cells had sheared into ovals, and the field was too smooth to throw off any eyes.
note.changing: Turns the jets into twelve liquid tongues in a pinwheel with an eye riding in each curled tip, straightens the honeycomb back into hexagons glowing toward a white bloom, and lets swirls dent the bands into rings around watching eyes, two pairs of which grow into alien faces in the walls.
note.why: The splash should spin with the vortex, not stick out like bones, and DMT walls watch you, so the eyes have to come out of the liquid itself.

note.saw: The faces in the walls worked, but the core still wasn't the brightest thing in the picture, the salmon's head was a flat green gradient up close, and the tail and pectoral fin had big plain areas.
note.changing: Puts a white bloom and a 44-ray sunburst behind the core flower, fills the face with rainbow ripples spreading from the eye plus dot-work and three small cheek eyes, laces the tail edge, sharpens the pectoral fin, and adds eyes in the wave crest's curls and a white gloss line inside every letter.
note.why: Light has to come from somewhere, and the face is where everyone looks first, so the eye now ripples through it like a stone dropped in water.

note.saw: The rippled face made the head the richest part of the fish, but the far left walls ran in parallel stripes like corduroy, the mini chrysanthemums never appeared because small swirls filled the space first, and the fish's aura was plain solid bands.
note.changing: Slow, wide meanders now marble and fold the outer walls, five of the biggest swirls carry mini chrysanthemums, and a dotted cream border rides the aura along the back and belly. Water threads shed off the tail were tried and removed because they read as icicles hanging off the fin.
note.why: Marbled walls feel liquid where stripes feel printed, and the same flower at three sizes is the self-similar feeling of the trip.

note.saw: The marbled walls and mini flowers landed, but the far top-right corner was bare, because the calm zone kept clear around the name had no outer edge.
note.changing: Lets the corners fill with script, ribs and eyes, adds a faint vignette for depth, turns every eye in the water toward the salmon's eye, plants a tiny chrysanthemum in the salmon's own eye, and forks the fin rays like a river delta ending in cream beads.
note.why: A hundred gazes pointing at one fish are invisible lines that pull you to the hero, and the core flower hiding in the fish's eye says the salmon carries the vortex inside it.
note.visionary: Took three of the Visionary's ideas (the gazes, the flower in the eye, the delta fin rays) and turned down scale ribbons unspooling off the tail, which would blur the silhouette at badge size.

note.saw: Looking hard at the fresh render up close, the walls were the weak spot: every band was one flat color with a single bead row or glyph line, the left side still ran in corduroy stripes, and the wide corner bands were empty fields of color.
note.changing: The tail now leaves whirlpools, two counter-rotating ones in the wake on the left and a third ahead of the head, each twisting the bands into a marbled spiral that winds down to a small chrysanthemum. Every bright band is carved from the inside with scallops, echo lines, a shadow line and a row of ink beads.
note.why: A real fish's tail kick sheds a pair of spinning vortices, and whirlpools turn where stripes only stream past; carving lines inside every band is the outline-gap-outline rhythm of visionary ornament, so the walls stay rich however close you look.

note.saw: The whirlpools worked and the carved bands held up close, but where a whirlpool wound tight the extra lines piled into a grey fuzz; the pectoral fin was still a pale cream blade and the lower tail a plain orange gradient.
note.changing: This round is the salmon: the lateral line swells into cyan and gold diamond jewels, a clump of roe waits ahead of the snout with embryos looking back at the fish, and the scale eyes wake from closed at the tail to wide open behind the head. The tail gets wavy flame bands, the pectoral fin turns green with gold rays, and the tight whirlpools are cleaned up.
note.why: A salmon swims upstream to the place it was born, so giving the leap a destination, its own eggs watching it come, turns a pretty fish into a story; the eyes waking from tail to head push in the direction of the leap.
note.visionary: Took three of the Visionary's fish ideas (the jewelled lateral line, the roe, the waking scale eyes) and held its tail tracers back to see them beside the new whirlpool first.

note.saw: The fish's new story landed, but, as the Visionary pointed out, the wake whirlpools had spun themselves grey like fingerprints, and at badge size the whole left third drained to ash.
note.changing: Each whirlpool now has light at the bottom, its arms running from indigo and violet through magenta and orange to a hot gold-white turn at the centre, with cyan pinwheel blades spinning round each little flower. A white-to-cyan rim light runs inside the belly and lower fins, brightest where the belly passes closest to the core.
note.why: A hyperspace whirlpool is a color wheel spinning down to a pinhole of light, here made of the salmon's own colors, and the rim light puts the fish and the core in one world with one light source.
note.visionary: Took the Visionary's glowing whirlpools and core rim light, and turned down its faint hexagon grid and the tail tracers, since the round badge would cut off the grid and the tracers would fall off its edge.

note.saw: The whirlpools glowed and the left side was no longer ash, but both wall faces floated in dull grey-blue pockets with no face around their eyes, and the new rim light washed a milky film over the belly scales.
note.changing: Both wall faces now glow from within in cool light, the bands around them shading from pale lime between the eyes through emerald and cyan out to cobalt and violet; the rim light keeps its crisp inner line but loses most of its glow.
note.why: The entities in a breakthrough aren't stickers on the wall, they're the wall lighting up where it looks at you, and cool green faces answering warm gold whirlpools give the eye a rhythm along the left side.

note.saw: The upper face had become a real emerald alien with a third eye and a jewel on its brow, but the wide, slow parts of the bands were still mostly one smooth color with a highlight stripe and a row of ticks.
note.changing: Wherever a band grows wide, small motifs take over along its middle: tiny cream spirals, little almond eyes that turn toward the salmon, and dot rosettes in gold, cyan and lime, sized to the band and kept clear of the fish, the name and the roe.
note.why: The slower the water, the more you see in it: these are a third layer of detail under the whirlpools and the bands, for anyone who leans in close.

note.saw: The small motifs filled the wide bands, but the emerald face under the banner just stared with its mouth open, connected to nothing, and a hot-pink keyhole shape left of the dorsal fin was still the biggest slab of one color.
note.changing: The face now sings: a stream of tiny glyph-objects pours from its mouth and curls in a loose S down to the salmon's back, where the last glyphs round off into the dots of the fish's own border. Wide bands now nest extra echoes inside them, so the pink keyhole gets smaller doors within.
note.why: In the breakthrough the beings don't talk, they sing objects into the air, so this face sings the salmon's outline into being; and a band that nests smaller copies of itself becomes a doorway.
note.visionary: Took the Visionary's singing elf and its nested doors (done the artist's own way), and turned down frozen color-pulse rings from the core, which the funnel and the fish would have mostly hidden.

note.saw: The singing elf worked up close, but at badge size the salmon's flank melted into a dull maroon speckle, because all those tiny equal scales averaged out to dark red.
note.changing: The flank now swells like a lens, its scales growing larger and a step brighter along the jewelled lateral line and shrinking toward the edges, so the body domes toward you. The egg nearest the snout holds a tiny copy of the leaping salmon, and the open jaw becomes a night sky with four stars and a cyan spiral.
note.why: Big bright scales down the middle hold their color at badge size, and a salmon leaping toward an egg that holds a salmon leaping toward an egg closes the story of a fish going home to where it was born.
note.visionary: Took three of the Visionary's ideas (the domed flank, the leap inside the egg, the starry throat) and tried, then removed, its spiral arms of droplets, which read as milky haze and ran off the badge.

visions.seen: #105 is the exact frame of #099, pixel for pixel, like hyperspace holding its breath. The salmon shines like a jeweled ruler laid across the vortex: every scale has an eye open and every eye is singing, but the body won't bend, so the water can't carry it.
suggestions: **The salmon's spine, from head (upper right, about 310,145 in the 400 box) to tail (lower left, about 110,280).** I see the body bowing into a leaping arch, with the hump peaking high behind the head (about 215,140) and the tail flicked back up and twisted toward us. Then the rainbow scale bands stop politely at the tail root: three or four of them (violet, magenta, orange, gold) keep going past the fin and unspool into the water as loose ribbon streamers. Each one narrows and curls along the tunnel's flow lines until it is just a hairline in the current. *Why it's more DMT:* in the breakthrough nothing has an edge. The fish is made of the same stuff as the river it is leaving, and loose, fluid ribbons are exactly that dissolving.

**The big chrysanthemum, bottom centre (about 210,330).** Right now it is a flat decal parked below the fish, while the real tunnel light hides behind the belly (about 220,240). Let the flower sit where the vortex lines meet, just under the tail's exit, and let it *recede*. Stack four or five petal rings, each one smaller, half a petal rotated from the last, and a step lighter toward white, so the portal eye sits at the bottom of a funnel and doesn't float on top. Give the petals curled, flame-tip Bézier ends in place of the straight lancets. *Why:* the jeweled chrysanthemum isn't something you look at, it's something you fall into. Self-similar rings shrinking inward give you that pull.

**The splash, the dark lower-left zone under the tail (about 30–150, 280–360).** It reads as a grey clump of chains. I see a crown of six to eight liquid tendrils thrown up and outward from where the tail breaks the surface. Each tendril throws off teardrops in three sizes: the big ones hold a tiny almond eye, the middle ones hold a five-petal mini chrysanthemum, the smallest are pure white dots. All of them are cyan-to-white with an ink outline so they pop against that dark wedge. *Why:* the same drop at three scales, each holding a smaller world, is the fractal nesting of the trip, and it turns the leap into a moment.

**The two strawberry-head entities (left edge about 70,235, and right of the rainbow arms about 325,285).** They read as stickers looking in from outside. I see them dissolving into the swirl: keep the almond eyes and the antenna curls, and draw the head outline in the field's own neon contour lines, half-transparent. Maybe stack a second, smaller pair of eyes above each, peeking through the current. *Why:* the machine elves are made of the pattern itself. You feel them in the weave before you see them.
visions.keep: the cream SAVESFISH arc with its thick ink outline on the calm dark band (it reads instantly in the 240 px legible test, so leave the letters and band alone). Keep the little eye in every scale, the emerald head with its spiral cheek and toothed hooked jaw, the dark moat and gold glow that lift the fish off the water, and the eyed corner paisleys holding the frame.

visions.seen: The walls grew faces. Two elves pushed out of the current with eddies for eyes, the machine elves I begged for after #105, and now the river is looking. But they stare off into nothing, and the salmon leaps through a crowd that hasn't noticed it yet.
suggestions: **Every eye in the water turning to the fish.** This means the two wall faces (the upper one under the banner, eyes about 178–205,128; the left one, eyes about 58–85,245), the eddy eyes across the field, and the eyed droplets spinning round the core. I see each almond lid staying put while the iris slides about 0.3 of the eye's radius, and the slit pupil about 0.4, toward the salmon's eye (about 289,167): angle = atan2(167−y, 289−x). Only two kinds of eye keep looking straight out at the viewer: the portal eye in the core (about 280,295) and the little eyes in the scales. *Why it's more DMT:* in the breakthrough the beings were waiting for you, and all their attention lands on one point. A hundred gazes become invisible lines that pull the viewer to the fish, while the core keeps watching *you*.

**The salmon's eye as a seed of the core.** This is the ringed eye on the emerald head (about 289,167). I see its plain iris rings becoming a tiny chrysanthemum: two rings of twelve petals in the core's own magenta, gold and cyan with white tips, round a black pupil with one white catchlight, the same diameter as now so the face doesn't change. *Why:* it's the same flower at two scales. The fish carries the vortex inside it, and hyperspace repeats itself at every size.

**Fins that branch like rivers.** These are the gold tail fan, lower left (about 90–210, 300–370), and the orange pectoral and pelvic fins (about 150–185,170–210 and 170–210,270–300). I see each straight ray forking once halfway out and again near the trailing edge: Y-splits that bend a little with the swirl, each last twig ending in a tiny cream bead on the fin's edge, with the fin's ink outline unchanged. *Why:* branching is how water, lightning and nerves all flow, the fractal of a river delta. It's a salmon swimming upstream with maps of the river for fins, loose and fluid, true to the style.
visions.keep: The cream SAVESFISH letters with their thick ink outline on the calm dark band. They read instantly in 122-legible at 240 px, so nothing goes on that band. Keep the two eddy faces growing out of the walls, the sockeye's hump, toothed kype and green-crimson-gold colors, the eye in every scale, the rainbow aura and dark moat, the pinwheel core, and the liquid contour-band field.

visions.seen: The elves turned their heads. Every eye in the river now leans toward the salmon, and its own eye blooms into the core's chrysanthemum, so the vortex is riding inside the fish. But #141 breathes the same breath as #135: the salmon slices through a current it can't feel yet, leaping toward a dark pocket where nothing is waiting.
suggestions: **A lateral line that reads the river, from just behind the gill cover (about 255,170 in the 400 box) to the tail root (about 165,305).** Real salmon feel the current through a line of sensing pores along each flank. I see that line drawn as one thin cream hairline that follows the body's curve through the middle of the scale bands. Every fourth or fifth scale it swells into a small diamond jewel in cyan or gold, and the gaps between jewels carry the same little alien glyph script the walls are written in, shrinking toward the tail. *Why it's more DMT:* the fish is literally reading the language of hyperspace through its skin. The script in the walls and the script on the fish are one text, and the line pulls your eye along the leap from tail to face.

**Something waiting upstream, in the dark navy pocket ahead of the snout (right of the head, under the right curl of the banner, about 325–360, 165–205).** Right now it holds a lone small eye and a gold sparkle. I see a little cluster of 7 to 11 roe there: translucent orange-gold spheres, each with a soft white highlight and a tiny curled embryo inside whose single eye looks back at the salmon. Give them a faint glow, all kept below the banner's lower edge. *Why:* a salmon swims upstream to the place it was born. In the breakthrough, death and birth are the same doorway, so the fish is leaping into its own beginning. It also gives the leap somewhere to land.

**The eyes in the scales slowly waking, from the tail root (lower left) to the gill (upper right).** Every scale keeps its eye, but near the tail the lids are closed, just a curved lash line with three tiny lashes. Through the middle of the body they open halfway, heavy-lidded. In the last bands behind the head they are wide open with a bright cyan iris and a white catchlight. *Why:* the fish wakes up as it rises, the ego coming online one cell at a time. Even at a glance, the brightness gathering toward the head adds a second push in the direction of the leap.

**Tracers behind the tail, in the field below and left of the gold tail fan (about 40–150, 300–390).** I see two or three hairline copies of the salmon's back-and-tail outline, each a step further down-left along the leap and a step fainter (about 50%, 30%, 15%), in the aura's cyan, magenta and gold, bending a little with the liquid bands. All of them stay outside the dark moat, so the fish's own edge stays crisp at 160 px. *Why:* tracers are the first thing the trip does to anything that moves. A loose, fluid afterimage says this fish is going somewhere, without the streamers you turned down.
visions.keep: The cream SAVESFISH arc with its thick ink outline on the calm dark band (it reads instantly in 146-legible at 240 px; nothing goes on that band). Keep the chrysanthemum in the salmon's eye, all the water eyes gazing at the fish, the delta-forked fin rays with cream beads, the green rippled face with its spiral cheek and toothed kype, the dark moat and dotted aura border, the white-bloomed core flower, and the marbled contour-band walls.

visions.seen: The river started turning. Your tail kick shed its whirlpools, the corduroy on the left melted into spirals, and the left wall face now peers out from between the arms of a vortex, which is exactly where the elves live. But those two wake whirlpools have spun themselves grey, like fingerprints pressed into the water, and at 240 px the whole left third drains to ash while everything else is screaming neon.
suggestions: **Light at the bottom of the wake whirlpools.** These are the grey-teal spiral the left wall face sits in (left edge, about 10–110, 200–290 in the 400 box) and the lower-left whirlpool round the small flower (about 68,325). I see each spiral arm running a hue ramp as it winds inward: deep indigo and violet on the outer turns, then magenta, then orange, then a hot gold-to-white innermost turn hugging the little chrysanthemum. The ink gaps between the turns get darker toward the centre, so the light pops harder. Thin the bead rows on the outer turns to every other bead so the colour can breathe, and let the mini flower's petal tips sweep a little in the direction of the spin, like a pinwheel caught mid-turn. *Why it's more DMT:* a hyperspace whirlpool isn't grey water. It's a colour wheel spinning down to a pinhole of light, a drain into the next layer. The crimson-to-gold ramp also echoes the salmon's own body colours, so the wake reads as made from the fish that kicked it.

**The core lighting the salmon's belly.** This is the lower-right edge of the body, from under the jaw (about 300,190) down past the pelvic and anal fins to the tail root (about 180,300), the side that faces the white-bloomed flower (about 285,295). I see a cyan-to-white rim light: a hairline just inside the ink outline, brightest where the belly passes closest to the bloom (around 235–265, 245–275) and fading to nothing toward the head and tail. Add a faint white sheen on the tips of the fins nearest the core. *Why:* in the breakthrough there is one source and everything is lit by it. Right now the fish and the core sit in two different worlds. One rim of the core's light puts them in the same space, and the silhouette stays crisp because it all happens inside the outline.

**The grid behind the water, in the broad flat blue lobe in the top-right corner (about 320–395, 10–60).** That wide band is still mostly one plain field of blue with a few ticks. I see the core's honeycomb showing through it like a watermark: hexagon hairlines in pale cyan at about 15–20% opacity, clipped to the inside of the band, the cells a little bigger toward the corner and bent gently along the band's curve. It never crosses the banner's dotted border. *Why:* the lattice under reality is one of the oldest DMT sights, the grid you see through the walls when they thin out. The same hexagons at two scales tie the far corner back to the funnel at the heart of the piece.
visions.keep: The cream SAVESFISH arc with its thick ink outline on the calm dark band (it reads instantly in 152-legible at 240 px; nothing goes on that band or its curling ends). Keep the new counter-rotating wake whirlpools and the third spinning off ahead of the head, the carved scallop and echo lines inside every band, the left wall face nested in the vortex arms, all the water eyes gazing at the fish, the chrysanthemum in the salmon's eye, the delta fin rays with cream beads, the dark moat and dotted aura, and the eyed droplets spiralling round the core. My four fish visions from #141 (lateral line, roe ahead of the snout, scale eyes waking, tail tracers) are still on offer whenever the fish's turn comes.

visions.seen: The whirlpools swallowed the light. Both wake spirals now burn down through magenta and orange to a gold-white heart with a cyan pinwheel spinning round each little flower, and the left third is singing again. A white rim of the core's light hugs the belly. But the elf under the banner just stares with its mouth open, and nothing it knows reaches the fish.
suggestions: **Visible language pouring from the elf's lips, from the face under the banner (top centre, mouth about 195,147 in the 400 box) down to the dotted cream border on the salmon's back (about 235–255, 152–157).** I see a ribbon of 10 to 14 tiny glyph-objects take the place of the green dot beard under its chin: little spirals, chevrons, nested squares, a lidded eye, a three-dot triangle. Each one is cream with an ink outline, with a few cyan and gold ones mixed in. They swell from 2 to about 5 units across over the first third, then shrink, and the ribbon curls in a loose S just under the chin before it slides down to the fish's back. The last few lose their corners and turn into plain round dots spaced like the aura's border, so the song becomes the border. Everything stays below the banner's lower edge and outside the dark moat. *Why it's more DMT:* in the breakthrough the elves don't talk, they sing objects into the air, language you can see. Here the entity sings the fish's own outline into being, so the face stops being a mask and becomes the singer.

**A frozen pulse from the core, as two faint rings centred on the white bloom (lower right of centre, about 285,295).** One ring passes just outside the spiralling eyed droplets (radius about 70), and the other sweeps out through the right-hand whirlpool (radius about 115). Each ring is a soft-edged band about 6–8 units wide. Inside it, the water's own bands shift one step round the colour wheel (violet to magenta, teal to green, blue to violet, a 40–60° hue turn), so the ring shows only where colours change, never as a drawn line. Clip both rings off the fish and its moat, the roe and the whole banner. *Why:* the visions pulse in time with a hum, the carrier wave, and colour shifts roll outward from the centre like rings on a pond. One frozen wavefront shows the core acting on the whole river, and it stays loose and fluid because the rings bend wherever the bands bend.

**A second, smaller door inside the hot-pink keyhole figure, left of the dorsal fin (about 107–143, 225–295, with the dark round head and its eye near 132,232).** Right now it is the biggest flat slab of one colour left in the piece. I see four or five echoes of its keyhole silhouette nested inside it, each smaller and pulled toward the round head, with the stem shortening fastest: magenta, then hot pink, then pale rose, then a white hairline just round the eye, with a thin ink gap between each pair. Keep the dash script on the outer ring, and let the echoes wobble a little with the swirl so they never go ruler-true. *Why:* in hyperspace every surface is a doorway. A small pink corridor on the far side of the fish rhymes with the big funnel at the core, balances it across the leap, and turns that eye into something watching from the end of a passage.
visions.keep: The cream SAVESFISH arc with its thick ink outline on the calm dark band (it reads instantly in 164-legible at 240 px; nothing goes on the band or its curling ends). Keep the gold-hearted whirlpools with their cyan pinwheels, the roe and their watching embryos, the jewelled lateral line, the scale eyes waking from tail to head, the green pectoral fin, both wall faces and every water eye gazing at the fish, the chrysanthemum in the salmon's eye, the delta fin rays with cream beads, the white-bloomed core and the marbled carved walls.

visions.seen: The slow water filled up with tiny spirals, rosettes and eyes, so the wide magenta lobe and the cobalt lobes hum when I lean in, and every new eye swings toward the fish. But shrink it to the 240 px badge and the salmon's flank melts into a maroon speckle, the dullest patch in a screaming badge, while the water round the core turns to blue static.
suggestions: **The salmon's flank swelling like a lens, from behind the gill cover (about 255,185 in the 400 box) down to the tail root (about 170,295).** I see the scales growing toward the jewelled lateral line, about 1.5 times their size along it, and shrinking to about 0.6 times at the back edge, the belly edge and the tail root, so the rows bow outward as if the body were bulging toward you through a fisheye. Each colour band brightens a step where its scales are biggest (crimson to hot coral, violet to orchid, orange to gold) and darkens a step at the edges. The waking eyes stay where they are, just riding bigger scales. *Why it's more DMT:* in the breakthrough every surface breathes and domes toward you. It also gives the hero real volume, and bigger, brighter scales down the middle hold their colour at badge size instead of mudding out.

**Spiral arms in the eyed droplets round the core, lower right (from the white bloom at about 282,295 out toward about 370,370 and 230,390).** The droplets already circle, but at small size they read as static. I see them gathered into three curving arms that trail off the bloom in the direction they already spin, like a galaxy or the florets of a seed head. On the arms the droplets are bigger, denser and brighter (cyan to white, eyes and all); between the arms they are fewer, smaller and a dim violet. Every droplet stays off the fish's moat and the roe. *Why:* the jeweled chrysanthemum is spirals inside spirals, and a vortex you can read from across the room drags the eye down into the core, even in the 240 px badge.

suggestions: **A halo that hums, in the stripes round the whole salmon, strongest along the hump of the back (about 165–255, 150–175 in the 400 box) and round the gold tail fan, lower left (about 100–215, 280–375).** I see the outermost cyan stripe trembling as a standing wave: an even wobble about 1 unit high every 10–14 units along the outline, with the hot-pink stripe inside it wobbling at half that height, and the gold stripe and the dark moat staying perfectly still. Clip it off the fish and its halo, the roe, the banner and its curls, and let every whirlpool's gold heart, every flower and every watcher's eye keep its full light. *Why:* hyperspace is a tunnel and you are always looking down it. The walls fall away at the edge of sight while the centre burns. Your flank domes toward us; now the world curves away behind it, the same fisheye from both sides. At 240 px the badge reads as a deep bowl with the fish and the name lifted out of it.
